article.headline: Scores from last Night: Clinton girls stay perfect; Ripley boys take first loss
article.html:
Clinton’s girls kept their perfect soccer record intact while handing Northwest Rankin its first reported loss Monday, and Brandon stopped West Lauderdale’s unbeaten girls start as part of a soccer sweep. On the basketball court, Itawamba Agricultural held off Ripley to end the Tigers’ perfect opening.

November 23, 2026, also brought first defeats for Oxford’s girls, Madison-Ridgeland Academy’s boys and Ocean Springs’ boys. Booneville, West Union and Potts Camp protected unbeaten basketball records. Below are selected verified varsity finals, with records as currently listed on the completed matchup reports.

Clinton girls win the unbeaten soccer matchup

Clinton beat Northwest Rankin 1–0 in girls soccer and is listed at 5–0. The match was scoreless at halftime before the Arrows scored the only goal after the break. Northwest Rankin is 5–1–1 after its first reported defeat, settling the unbeaten meeting featured in our Monday Games To Watch preview.

The boys teams finished level at 1–1. Northwest Rankin is listed at 3–3–1 and Clinton at 2–3–2. The schools therefore ended the soccer doubleheader with a Clinton girls victory and a boys draw.

Brandon shuts out West Lauderdale in both divisions

Brandon’s girls won 2–0 against West Lauderdale, scoring once in each half. The Bulldogs are listed at 7–3, while the Knights are 8–1 after their first reported loss. West Lauderdale had brought a perfect record into the nonconference match, but Brandon kept the visitors off the scoreboard throughout.

The Bulldogs’ boys followed with a 6–0 victory, putting three goals on the board in each half. Brandon is listed at 4–4–1 and West Lauderdale at 5–5–1. Both Brandon teams won without allowing a goal.

Jackson Prep ends Oxford’s perfect start; Itawamba edges Ripley

Jackson Prep beat Oxford 43–35 in girls tournament basketball. The Patriots are listed at 6–2, with the Chargers at 6–1 after their first reported defeat. Oxford had entered the matchup without a loss, making Prep’s win one of the notable changes to the early unbeaten records in this selection.

Itawamba Agricultural defeated Ripley 49–45 in boys basketball. The Indians are listed at 2–4 and the Tigers at 4–1 after their first loss. Ripley outscored Itawamba 23–13 in the third quarter, but the Indians took the fourth 10–7 to finish the game ahead.

Mooreville won the girls game against Ripley 73–43. The Troopers are listed at 5–3 and the Tigers at 4–2. Together, the finals left Ripley without a victory in its reported Monday varsity basketball games.

MRA and Ocean Springs boys take first defeats

Houston, Tennessee, beat Madison-Ridgeland Academy 80–62. The Mustangs from Germantown are listed at 4–0, while MRA is 3–1. The result preserved Houston’s unbeaten start and ended the Patriots’ perfect opening in the interstate meeting.

Ocean Springs lost 57–49 to Hewitt-Trussville, Alabama, in a neutral-site boys tournament game. The Greyhounds are listed at 7–1 after their first reported defeat; Hewitt-Trussville is 3–2. Ocean Springs’ opening run ended against an out-of-state opponent after it had stayed perfect through the weekend.

Booneville stays unbeaten in both basketball divisions

Booneville’s girls beat Center Hill 58–25 and are listed at 3–0. The Blue Devil boys followed with a 65–50 win over New Hope and are 2–0. Center Hill’s girls are 3–3, and New Hope’s boys are 1–1 after Booneville took both varsity games.

West Union rallies; Potts Camp wins comfortably

West Union beat Holly Springs 65–58 in a neutral-site boys tournament game to reach a listed 7–0. Holly Springs won the first quarter 19–14 and the second 17–16, but West Union took the third 24–12 and the fourth 11–10. The Eagles reversed the early scoring pattern after halftime to keep their record perfect.

Potts Camp defeated East Union 79–53 and is listed at 6–0. The Cardinals preserved their unbeaten start in the neutral-site game, while East Union is 1–4. The final gave Potts Camp a much wider cushion than West Union had in its win.

Pontotoc County: Cougars girls reach a listed 7–0

South Pontotoc’s girls beat Shannon 63–31 to remain unbeaten at a listed 7–0. Shannon is 1–4. The Cougars added another decisive final to their perfect opening, while Pontotoc’s boys beat Florence, Alabama, 68–53 in a neutral-site tournament game and are listed at 4–1.

Saltillo beat North Pontotoc 62–57, leaving the Tigers listed at 1–3 and the Vikings at 6–3. Alcorn Central defeated South Pontotoc’s boys 48–41 in another reported tournament final. The Golden Bears outscored the Cougars 12–5 in the fourth quarter; their listed records are 2–3 and 4–3, respectively.

Corinth girls extend their winning run

Corinth beat Bayou Academy 58–47 at the Charger Basketball Invitational in Oxford. The Warriors are listed at 5–1 and Bayou at 3–6. Alcorn County Sports reports that Corinth has won four straight, giving the victory significance beyond the final margin.

Walnut holds off Belmont; Hickory Flat sweeps Falkner

Walnut’s boys edged Belmont 53–50. The Wildcats built a 24–13 first-quarter advantage, which proved valuable as Belmont outscored them 19–11 in the fourth. Walnut is listed at 5–1 and Belmont at 2–1 after the tournament game.

Wheeler beat Walnut’s girls 64–54. The Eagles are listed at 4–4 and the Wildcats at 7–2. Walnut therefore split its reported Monday varsity basketball results, with the boys winning narrowly and the girls taking a loss.

Hickory Flat beat Falkner 64–18 in boys basketball and won the girls game 57–38. The Rebels’ boys won every quarter and held Falkner to three points in the fourth. Hickory Flat’s listed records are 4–5 for the boys and 5–3 for the girls.

Nettleton defeated Blue Mountain 68–49 in boys basketball. The Tigers are listed at 6–1 and the Cougars at 4–4. For earlier area results, see our Saturday varsity recap.

DeSoto Central wins twice; Lake Cormorant edges Southaven

DeSoto Central’s girls beat North Panola 62–30 and its boys defeated Memphis Academy of Science and Engineering 56–42, both at neutral sites. The Jaguar girls are listed at 2–2 and boys at 3–2. The girls won every quarter, while the boys opened with a 17–7 first period and stayed ahead in the final scoring.

Lake Cormorant edged Southaven 45–43 in girls basketball and is listed at 5–1; the Chargers are 4–3. Cleveland Central won 42–33 against Horn Lake, leaving the Wolves at 7–1 and the Eagles at 6–2.

Hancock girls reach 7–0

Hancock’s girls beat Tupelo 50–41 and remain unbeaten at a listed 7–0. The Golden Wave are 1–3. The Hawks joined Booneville and South Pontotoc among the girls basketball teams that protected perfect records in these verified finals.

Soccer sweeps for Center Hill and Amory

Center Hill beat Southaven 3–1 in girls soccer and won the boys match 2–0. The Mustang boys scored once in each half and are listed at 6–3; their girls are 3–5. Southaven’s corresponding records are 5–3–1 for the boys and 5–5 for the girls.

Amory beat Lafayette 2–1 in girls soccer and won the boys match 1–0. All three goals in the girls game came before halftime, with neither team scoring afterward. The Panthers’ girls are listed at 5–4 and boys at 7–2–1. Lafayette’s girls are 5–1–2 after their first reported defeat; its boys are 2–6.
